summary:
The Public Ministry's 2012–2021 study places La Libertad second in absolute LGTB-homicide count (10 of 88 — after Lima's 12, level with Lima Norte), centred on Trujillo. The region's population share (~3%) is far smaller than its death share (~11.4%), giving a per-capita lethality roughly 3.8× the national average — a materially concerning concentration not explained by population alone, and placing the unit below the national score (0.36).

Counterweight: Ordenanza Regional N.° 009-2024-GRLL-CR (regional session 3 September 2024, approved 6 September 2024, published in El Peruano November 2024) promotes labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender people — their right to formal, dignified work in equitable conditions without discrimination on gender identity or expression, and recognition of the trans community as a vulnerable group. This is a resident-facing instrument (a visitor does not use it), but it evidences that this particular regional council legislated visibly for trans inclusion — the one such ordinance found in Peru's 26 departments. It also sits in the same department where rondas campesinas exercise recognised dispute-resolution authority, a structural caveat with no documented trans-specific case.

Net deviation: −0.02 from national. The per-capita violence concentration is the dominant factor; the ordinance prevents a larger deduction. vs Lima (now 0.38, above national): La Libertad's per-capita lethality remains worse, though Lima's higher absolute count and 2025 reporting case have lifted its score since the original comparison. vs Tacna (0.34): both are modestly below national, but La Libertad's multi-year dataset is more robust evidence than a single incident.

sources.summary: Public Ministry press note (23 Mar 2022) for its study of intentional killings of LGTB people, Jan 2012–May 2021: 84 criminal complaints covering 88 victims and 72 accused; 58% of deaths in six fiscal districts (Lima 12, La Libertad 10, Lima Norte 10, Lima Este 7, Lima Sur 6, Callao 6); victims mostly gay men (55.8%) and trans women (36.4%), adults 25–54 (72.7%), 94.3% Peruvian nationals; perpetrators mostly men (94.4%), known or family (26.4%) or partners/ex-partners (26.4%); 47.7% occurred in victims' own homes; case-file motive recorded common crime (21.6%) with no motive data in 45.5%, but press-review analysis estimates 68.9% show bias-violence indicators. Study by the Public Ministry observatory with Justice Ministry and Cayetano Heredia observatory, UNDP support.

Regional government of La Libertad: Ordenanza Regional N.° 009-2024-GRLL-CR — approved at regional council session 3 September 2024 (6 September 2024), promotes labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender people in the region; guarantees the right to formal, dignified, productive work in equitable conditions without discrimination on gender identity or its expression, and recognises the trans community as a group in a situation of vulnerability.

Official gazette text of Ordenanza Regional N.° 000009-2024-GRLL-CR, Trujillo, 6 September 2024: full ordinance promoting labour inclusion of travestis, transsexuales and transgénero in the La Libertad Region; grounded in the Political Constitution (equality and non-discrimination articles) and the regional-government framework (decentralisation laws 27680/27783/27867); issued under the region's ordinance-making competence.

outOfScopeNotes: Community self-governance (rondas campesinas dispute-resolution authority in parts of the department) is structural context relevant to general order, not trans-specific: no documented trans case involving it. General crime and political instability affect all travellers; the assessment reflects trans-specific risk only.
tangentialFactors: The 2012–2021 LGTB homicide dataset (88 deaths) is majority gay men (55.8%); trans women account for 36.4% (about 32 cases). The regional concentration is real for trans people but the headline count is LGB-heavy — a rater should read the trans share directly rather than inherit the total.
localsOnly: The regional labour-inclusion ordinance (Ordenanza 009-2024-GRLL-CR) protects resident workers in formal employment; a visitor does not use it.
